POLISH-001.notes: Latency guard recalibrated twice on 2026-10-14. First pass: `plan_generation_stays_fast_on_the_reference_pack` asserted a single 1000 ms bound on the first plan build in the process, but that first build also reads the pack from cold pages (the parse cache is per version root and every test installs a fresh store), so the number measured the runner and its page cache — it passed at 10.8 ms warm on the 2026-10-04 baseline and failed at 1.447 s cold on a 2-core CI runner (run 38624968580). Second pass the same day: the replacement absolute repeat bound (`<600 ms`) went red on a contended runner at 796 ms beside a 787 ms cold build (run 38650579941, head `2dbf04a`, an evidence-only change; desktop lib binary 2,752 s for 139 tests), while identical code was green four minutes earlier in run 38645447729. Final guard: non-empty plan for a five-minute budget, identical item count for the same clock reading, cold build under 8 s, repeat build at most 1.25 times that process's own cold cost, plus a 4 s gross-cost backstop. Measured after the change: cold 289.4 ms / warm 92.7 ms (bound 361 ms, 3.9x headroom), focused test ok in 134.23 s, fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean. Stated limitation: wall-clock on a shared runner cannot prove the parse cache was still hit — a full cache loss leaves warm roughly equal to cold, which the ratio bound passes; the user-visible latency promise is enforced on the real surface by the walkthrough's per-route stall guard.

INSTALL-UX-001.title: Installs have real progress, failure recovery, and a receipt
INSTALL-UX-001.summary: Pack install is bounded and honest: real progress, cancel/retry/resume, a receipt, and an explicit decision on pre-archived bundles.
INSTALL-UX-001.notes: Transport hardening is done (PACK-DL-ALLOWLIST-001). Implemented 2026-10-15: `engine-progress` carries a measured fetch percent from the pinned `PackEntry.size_bytes`, `verify`/unpack are named as unmeasurable rather than faked, cancel is honoured at chunk/redirect/phase boundaries (`cancel_pack_install` + `INSTALL_CANCEL`), and an `InstallReceipt` (pack/version/source host/sha256/size/capabilities) reaches the UI with Cancel and Retry. The second slice the same day closed both disclosed gaps: `lts_langpack::archive::install_with_cancel` takes a hook consulted per archive entry and again before the store is touched, and because extraction is staging-then-rename an abort leaves no version directory and never moves the `current` pointer; a cancelled transfer keeps its bytes in `partial-<key>.part` beside a sidecar naming url/sha256/size, so a retry sends `Range: bytes=<n>-`, adopts the prefix only on a `206`, and still checks the completed file against the pinned size and SHA-256 before the pack gate sees it — a `200` answer, a corrupt or foreign sidecar, or an oversized part restarts from zero. `install_from_catalog_report` refuses an install that cannot fit (free space from `statvfs` on unix, skipped rather than guessed elsewhere) and names a disk that fills during unpack. The renderer offers Cancel during fetch/verify/install and its copy now says a retry continues where it stopped. Still open and owner-gated: the measured timing half of issue #1 item I05 (fresh-artifact install and resume timed separately on the tiers `PERF-002` freezes) needs a published artifact, and the pre-archived-bundle question stays an owner decision. Evidence: state/evidence/INSTALL-UX-001/ENGINE-SLICE-2026-10-15.md, state/evidence/INSTALL-UX-001/RESUME-CANCEL-PREFLIGHT-2026-10-15.md.

SEC-001.title: Security/privacy release audit
SEC-001.summary: Malicious-pack suite, no unexpected speech upload in local mode, and secrets/logging/recording-retention gates all pass.
SEC-001.notes: Recorded 2026-10-15 (REL-001 recheck): required for desktop 1.0, previously ROADMAP-only, so docs/15 derivation reported it ready. The automated work on record is explicitly **partial** (2026-10-06 artifact): `cargo audit` across 528 crates (0 vulnerabilities, 2 warnings — an unmaintained build-time proc macro and a transitive glib unsoundness), a heuristic secret-pattern grep because gitleaks was not installed, and a manual licence audit. What the acceptance bullets additionally require is not covered by that artifact: the pack-install defences are enforced by tests that run today (`reference_audio_follows_the_manifest_and_refuses_traversal` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:11776`, `tampered_archive_is_rejected` and `redirect_hops_stay_on_allowlisted_hosts_for_downloads` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/packs.rs`), but there is no consolidated malicious-pack suite, no privacy review of provider upload paths, and no logging/recording-retention gate. Acceptance is a human disposition: an agent can run suites and record results, it cannot accept residual risk or sign off privacy. PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.title: A newer catalogue version of an installed pack is offered as an update
PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.summary: One installed-pack record feeds Home, the practice hub and the onboarding wizard, so a pack the catalogue lists at a different version is shown with both versions plus an update control wherever the learner already is.
PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.notes: Implemented 2026-10-17. `installedPacks: string[]` is gone from App.tsx and from OnboardingProps: the single record is `installed: InstalledPack[]` (App.tsx:320) filled by `refreshInstalled()` (App.tsx:931-942), which returns the records it read or null when the read failed and sets `installedUnknown` so the wizard still offers retry and Skip for now. Boot gained its own `catalog_packs` read in a separate try/catch (App.tsx:849-858) because `catalog` is otherwise empty during the wizard. The derived block (App.tsx:2840-2867) joins `available_version` onto each wizard row from `catalog` and derives `packUpdates` purely from entries whose non-null `installed_version` differs from `version`, so Home, the hub and Settings read one derivation. `updateFromCatalog(id)` (App.tsx:947-972) calls the same `install_catalog_pack` command Settings uses, then re-reads installed packs and the catalogue; `install(id)` re-checks through `refreshInstalled()` instead of fabricating a record, because `install_pack` returns a PackCandidate with no version (lib.rs:422-432) while `import_pack` (lib.rs:523) returns the full record. The wizard renders both versions in three states (stale, matching, no listed version) and the update control is a sibling of the untouched Install/Installed button; Continue is never disabled for a version mismatch. Learner copy never says newer or latest and never promises progress survives an update. Measured on GamingPC: `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `npx vitest run` 29 files / 253 tests (baseline 29 / 246), per-file counts 15->18 onboarding, 25->26 home, 3->4 hub, 10->10 a11y; `tools/audit_learner_copy.py` findings: 0. Criterion 2 rests on engine code unchanged here: the download re-verifies against the pin (packs.rs:846-900) and `crates/langpack/tests/media_upgrade.rs:161` keeps the previous version for rollback. `scripts/smoke-desktop.sh` stays owner-side because 127.0.0.1:1420 is held by the owner's running app.
